claims.claim: The character select screen has a strict 60-second time limit that cannot be raised in private games.

citations.review_text:
This is a review for the person who does not care about Solo Play.

Complete lack of any co-op vs NPC content

The PVP Netcode is terrible, no Rollback. This makes the any real attempts at getting out of combos in online games next to impossible due to how strict the timings are.

if there is an easier way, the tutorial needs to teach you this. I had to google how to transform for instance because in the forced tutorial at the beginning of the game that has no story relevence, they dont teach you how to go super saiyan. If youre going to force a tutorial, at LEAST teach people how to do one of the most iconic things in the series.

Theres a hard 60 second limit on character select, which when you can select 5 characters, theres like 100 and theres a 5 second animation that plays apon selection, you are really stretched for time, and you cannot raise it in even in private games.

It took so long for the base game to go on sale and not just the deluxe edition and I am sorely dissapointed, I just wanted to beat up my buddies online in private games but its not even good for that.

TLDR: 
Tutorial BAD 
Netcode BAD 
Lobby System BAD 
NO CO-OP CONTENT 
Gameplay pretty good, though.

if you played budokai tenkaichi 2 on the ps2 back then, this feels exactly like it. Although the story feels a bit meh and really quick, the gameplay is pretty much what you had back then with a bit more characters. A lot of buttom mashing, really quick fights and a bunch of action.

Unfortunately FPS are capped at 60, but other than that, no issues at all.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance drops and increased lag following recent updates and DLC releases, requiring lowered graphical settings.

citations.review_text:
I would love to recommend this game but at current state I can't.

The What-ifs in the story which was advertised feature is locked behind "normal" mode which is hard mode because AI stronger than you. The game also doesn't tell you conditions for what ifs but usually is beat X under X amount of minutes so if you are casual player don't expect to get many of those unless you find a guide how to cheese them.

After last patch 10th August 2026 the game is just not fun. Performance wise it runs worse than ever before. I needed to lower settings on my machine because the game was a lot more laggy than before.

AI is completely broken. Even on easy mode it's just countering you constantly and fights I could win before became frustrating.

The game has great promise with all these scenarios, arenas and characters but the execution is just trash. It's hyper focused on making the game hard but forgeting to make it fun.

I cannot recommend this game at all not until AI is fixed and performance gets better

I really didn't want to leave a negative review, because I love the Tenkaichi games and I think this is a good follow up, but with the new DLC coming out the performance for the game has went from decent to downright awful.
The game ran perfectly fine before I installed the DLC, but now, even with all of the settings turned down, the game runs terribly and it's become quite apparent that the DLC hasn't been optimised at all. This went from a game I enjoyed to one that I can't even play properly because the DLC is now hardwired into my copy.
Please, for love of everything that is good in this world, fix this issue.

I bought the Ultimate edition of this game on release and they have now removed the Ultimate Edition from the Steam page. They recently made a Legendary Edition that includes all the same things that the Ultimate Edition had, but it also includes the new NEO DLC for the same price that the Ultimate Edition was. This means that I would need to spend an additional $35+ to play the NEO DLC even though people who buy the current Legendary Edition would not. The Ultimate Edition and Legendary Edition are fundamentally the same thing, but Bandai Namco is trying to cheat early supporters of this game out of their money because they know they can.

Ultimate Edition buyers got scammed — Do NOT support this publisher!

DO NOT BUY. This is one of the most anti-consumer moves I have ever seen from a major publisher.

I bought the expensive Ultimate Edition, which explicitly promised access to future DLCs and the full experience. Now, with the new NEO update, they pulled a disgusting bait-and-switch:

They replaced the Ultimate Edition with a "Legendary Edition" at the exact same price point.

Ultimate Edition owners DO NOT get the new DLCs/content that should have been covered by our premium purchase.

We effectively paid top dollar at launch just to be downgraded to "second-class customers" while they demand even more money for content that should be ours.

To make matters worse, the game is still plagued by ongoing issues that the developers refuse to fix properly:

Horrible Balance & Exploit Culture: The online Ranked mode is still a mess of unpunished rage-quitting, broken tracking, and spammed exploits.

Dismal Matchmaking & Netcode: Frequent disconnections, input delays, and awful lobby management.

Lazy Story Mode Scenarios: Half-baked "What-If" routes that feel rushed and empty compared to what was advertised.

Bandai Namco treated their most loyal fans—the ones who spent $100+ upfront to support the game—like absolute cash cows. They rebranded the store pages, locked new content behind a paywall for early adopters, and expect us to pay TWICE for the full game.

Absolute corporate greed at its worst. Save your money and do not support these predatory tactics.

Rating: 0/10 — Pure Greed.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the online player matching and competitive matches as unbalanced, filled with tier-hooring, and dominated by the same small group of characters across matches.

citations.review_text: Multiplayer is extremely unbalanced and prone to tierhoring, Singleplayer is lackluster. There's like 8 different single player modes and it's just the same gameplay over and over dressed under different sauces. Only for diehard fans

Recent DLC is functionally unplayable. Systems are poorly implemented, unbalanced, and frustrating. Biggest issue is with difficulty. Game designers don't understand how to program enemy difficulty ranges. Previously, enemies were mindless punching bags with no counterplay, variation, or challenge. However, in the last update with the DLC,  they button read so well that it makes MKII blush. Enemies have reactions that border on inhuman, and have even less variation than before. 

Rush, sidestep, four-hit combo twice, repeat. If you attack, auto block, if you manage to hit, supercounter, if you fire a special (even in recovery animation) teleport or autoblock, if you charge for ult, rush. This is every. Single. Fight. Without fail. 

Also online play is still an unbalanced mess with the same five character appearing in all levels of play, with even causal matches feeling like a sweat-fest. I've begun to see Gogeta blue in my dreams at this point. If I saw someone roll up with Juice, Zarbon, Z-Trunks, or anyone who isn't a fusion I might actually cry. 

Finally, the new mode designed to make single player actually exist is pretty awful. There is no meaningful customization to your desired fighter, even though they attempted to create the illusion of one. It's a one dimensional point allocation system which, while technically improving elements of your fighter, feels unimpactful and boring. 

Once again, where SZ takes one step forward it makes eight flamboyant leaps backward. Enemies are more difficult now? Cool. But wait! The Saiyan's paw hath curled, now they're unplayable. There's new, extensive single player content? Well it's boring, lacking in depth, unbalanced, and frustrating at the best of times. They finally began incorporating costumes, even possessing meaningful character changes? Well there's like four, they're just for fan favorites, and they're pretty bland. 

Do NOT buy the DLC, and drop this garbage fire - best to wait until Xenoverse 3 comes in 2047 …

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the publisher delisted and replaced the initial high-tier bundles with new editions, excluding early buyers from the new DLC and requiring an additional purchase.

citations.review_text: I have had this Steam account for 19 years, and with almost 600 hours of this game on here and 225 hours on the Xbox! Dragon Ball: Sparking! ZERO is currently my most-played game on steam. I loved it so much that I supported it heavily from day one, pre-ordering the $230 Premium Collector's Edition on Xbox and buying the $110 Ultimate Edition here on Steam. I never thought I would write a negative review for a game I've poured this much time into, but the sheer corporate greed on display is egregious and completely unacceptable. Bandai Namco is punishing their most dedicated day one investors by forcing us to fork over another $35 for the new DLC. To add insult to injury, they completely delisted the Ultimate Edition and replaced it with a new "Legendary Edition" for the exact same price conveniently putting it on sale right away. In my opinion, the loyal people who pre-ordered and purchased the game at day one are basically paying for the people who never bought the game to get all this extra content for less than free. I do love this game, but in its current state, I cannot honestly and truthfully suggest it to anybody at the moment without feeling like a liar. It is a predatory slap in the face to loyal fans, and I refuse to recommend a game that treats its day one community like an open wallet. On top of everything else, the comedy of it all is that I don't even own the DLC I'm locked out of, but the computer AI is completely allowed to use it against me and beat my face in when i play custom tournaments.

this game has been dead for months but let's see if we can hose whatever remaining players out of another $35. I'd rather pay someone $35 to shove a "Super Limit-Breaking NEO Edition" fist up the ass of whoever thought this was a good idea. 

Content looks good otherwise but i cannot recommend this game unless you have money to burn/really love dragonball

♥♥♥♥ you bandai namco

This new DLC is a scam and completely ruined my hype for the update/DLC. I paid $120 for the ultimate version before and now they swapped it for this legendary version and made it the same price $120 ($90 sale) with neo added on. This is so greedy and I feel punished for pre-ordering the game, no wonder they didn't reveal the price until release day. I have never been so uninterested to play an update/DLC ever until now, the fact they just swapped it out like this is absolutely ridiculous, sneaky and unfair, yes I'm aware the ultimate edition listed what we would get, but now this legendary edition is $90 on sale $120 regular, meanwhile I paid $120 before? Such a slap in the face, just trying to grab more money out of people for no reason.
